title: The check that never casts
prompt: The nightly load holds back any day with an event id it can't read, so the carrier can send that day again. `can_load` is meant to catch those days before they're written, but the run still crashes on the sample. Fix it.
rules: A day loads whole or not at all: a day with an event id that can't be read as a number (after its first letter) is held back, and the run goes on with the next day.
Every other day is loaded with all its rows, repeats included, and `event_no` as the starter computes it.
A missing id isn't a read error: its event loads with a NULL `event_no`.
Columns and types: `event_id STRING, shipment_id STRING, load_date DATE, event_no INT`.
hints: Run the starter on the sample. Which line raises the error, and which day was it writing?
`can_load` calls `count()`. Does counting a day's rows need `event_no`?
Spark only casts when an action needs the value. Check with an action that reads every value, or catch the error where the write raises it.
explanation: `count()` only needs the number of rows, so Spark drops `event_no` from the work and never runs the cast. Every day passes the check, and the bad one fails later, in the write. A check has to make Spark compute what the write will: `batch.collect()` reads every value, so the cast runs and `CAST_INVALID_INPUT` is caught; a filter on `event_no` works too. Or skip the check and wrap the write itself in `try`: a failed write commits no files, so the day is simply missing. Detecting bad ids with `try_cast(...).isNull()` is close, but it also holds back a day with a missing id, which casts to NULL without an error. Removing only the bad rows breaks the rule that a day loads whole.
